introduction.title: What does it take to turn an equation into a prediction?
introduction.deck: A guide to the questions, results and limits of reverse physics.

general.heading: What would make an equation a theory?
paragraphs: An equation can describe how something changes without telling us everything we need to know. What can we prepare? What can we measure? Does the prediction agree with an experiment? Those questions need answers before an attractive equation becomes a useful physical theory.

This project asks which assumptions make each answer possible. It began with Weyl gravity, a proposed description of gravity, and grew into an investigation of the mathematics that connects equations to predictions.

general.heading: What is being worked out?
paragraphs: There are two connected questions. Which physical requirements distinguish possible theories of gravity? And which mathematical assumptions are needed to turn a description into a prediction?

For example, suppose a computer produces increasingly detailed pictures of a wave. Knowing that these pictures eventually agree is different from knowing how detailed a picture must be to meet a chosen accuracy. The latter gives a usable error guarantee.

general.heading: What have we learned?
paragraphs: In a particular wave model, an explicit error guarantee lets us construct a detector prediction using relatively modest mathematical assumptions. Removing that guarantee changes the mathematical existence problem, even though the wave and detector have not changed.

A separate model shows why checking positivity at every finite cutoff need not produce one acceptable state for the full continuum. Positivity here means that the mathematical rule for probabilities cannot assign negative values to the relevant tests. Both examples have precise restrictions; neither establishes a complete theory of gravity.

general.heading: How should you judge this work?
paragraphs: Look for the question, the assumptions, the actual conclusion and the evidence supporting it. AI systems have contributed substantially to the calculations, code and writing, with Asger Alstrup Palm as the accountable human contact. That makes independent checking and clear explanations especially important.

The current full gravity export fails a consistency check. A partial repair exists, but it has not passed all the required tests. The wave result can be read independently of that unfinished construction.

physics.heading: From a field equation to a physical prediction
paragraphs: The programme separates equations of motion from state selection, gauge reduction, probability, causal response and comparison with data. Pure-Weyl gravity supplies a demanding case study: a local or mode-level construction does not by itself establish a viable interacting quantum theory.
The additional question is mathematical: which assumptions about the state space and the representation of its elements are actually used to construct an observable?

physics.heading: The role of reverse mathematics
paragraphs: Reverse mathematics asks which axioms are sufficient for a theorem and, where possible, which are necessary. Here the input contract matters: a convergent sequence of wave data supplied with an error schedule is a different mathematical input from a sequence merely promised to converge.
This distinction concerns what the model supplies to the prediction procedure. It is not evidence that a laboratory instrument must implement a particular formal system.

physics.heading: Two results worth separating
paragraphs: For a fixed scalar wave and smeared detector on the circle, supplying convergence rates permits reconstruction over a weak arithmetic base. The rate-free reconstruction principle has the strength of arithmetic comprehension in the specified coding. The lower bound is already carried by a limiting amplitude at time zero; it is not generated by propagation.

In a separate reduced tensor model, finite spatial cutoffs admit positive covariance repairs that cannot approach a smooth full repair under the stated commutator and short-distance requirements. This does not settle positivity of the full metric theory.

physics.heading: The current physical boundary
paragraphs: The serialized full-complex differential fails direct nilpotency checks. A trace/ghost candidate repairs the two exposed blocks and satisfies the checked contraction identities, but full nilpotency, chain maps and cyclicity remain unverified.
Consequently the published export cannot currently justify the full Green/Hadamard transfer. No physical Hilbert space, scattering theory or unitarity result follows from the present repair.

mathematics.heading: Which assumptions does a prediction use?
paragraphs: A physical theorem combines assumptions about a model, a class of mathematical objects, and a system in which existence is asserted. The programme separates these choices before asking what is sufficient for a specified conclusion.

For the mathematical reader, the central example is a represented wave observable: rational approximations describe inputs and outputs, and their convergence information is part of the definition of the problem.

mathematics.heading: Existence with and without a rate
paragraphs: A Cauchy condition says that for each tolerance there is an index beyond which all approximants agree within that tolerance. A supplied modulus gives a function selecting suitable indices. In weak foundations, extracting such information is an additional mathematical task.

Reverse mathematics studies equivalences over a specified base theory. RCA₀ is the weak base used here for coded constructions; ACA₀ additionally allows sets defined by arithmetic predicates. These are systems of axioms, not accuracy levels.

mathematics.heading: What the example establishes
paragraphs: For the stated circle-wave representation, a supplied Cauchy modulus suffices for observable reconstruction in RCA₀. The rate-free principle WR is equivalent over RCA₀ to ACA₀. The lower bound uses one fixed profile and one fixed detector at time zero.

This specializes a standard scalar-completeness reversal. Its value here is to expose exactly where a physical-looking reconstruction problem inherits its logical strength. The infinite argument is a human proof with independently checked finite reductions, not a proof-assistant formalization.

mathematics.heading: What remains separate
paragraphs: The representation is essential. Changing what constitutes an input can change the logical classification without changing the displayed wave equation. This example proves no representation-independent axiom requirement for physics.

The larger gravity programme involves differential complexes and their contractions. The current exported differential has a nonzero square; partial contraction identities alone do not repair that failure. These algebraic issues are separate from the wave reconstruction theorem.

specialist.heading: Scope and contribution
paragraphs: The programme audits implications from physical assumptions and represented mathematical carriers to explicit obligations. Its reverse-mathematical component should be distinguished from characterization of a gravitational action by physical postulates.

The introductory entry points are a represented wave reconstruction comparison and a conditional reduced-tensor positivity separation. Neither is offered as a new general completeness theorem or a newly discovered ghost mechanism.

specialist.heading: Represented reconstruction
paragraphs: For the fixed rate-free principle WR on bounded Cauchy sequences of rational mean-zero chiral step pairs, RCA₀ proves WR ↔ ACA₀. With a supplied modulus, RCA₀ proves the corresponding reconstruction principle. A fixed profile and evaluation of a fixed tent detector at time zero already realize the reversal.

The contribution is the explicit observable-level reduction and input-contract comparison. Prerequisites for the detailed account are second-order arithmetic and represented analysis. Finite rational checks support the reduction; the infinite equivalence is not machine-formalized.

specialist.heading: Reduced positivity
paragraphs: For the specified standard-real reduced TT carrier, finite spatial cutoffs admit symmetric smooth covariance repairs preserving the commutator. The established lower bound on the smooth-repair seminorm prevents a uniform smooth full repair. The statement does not assume stationary or mode-diagonal corrections.
Transfer to the full metric complex is unavailable: the all-energy action-normalized tensor commutator has not been identified on an accepted full export.

specialist.heading: Current obstruction and reading order
paragraphs: The published graph differential has exact first-order square defects. A 12-coefficient trace/ghost candidate removes the two exposed blocks; corrected inclusion and projection satisfy pi=1, QH+HQ=1−ip, Hi=0 and pH=0. Full nilpotency, both chain-map identities and cyclicity remain open.

Read the wave question for its precise input/output distinction. Use the research atlas for historical artifacts and dependency structure, with the current correction taking precedence over earlier transfer claims.

wave.title: When does an approximation justify a prediction?
wave.deck: The same wave and detector, with two different kinds of input information.

general.heading: A wave and a detector
paragraphs: Imagine a wave travelling around a circular track. Our mathematical detector returns a weighted average of the wave over space, rather than its height at one point. The example asks whether increasingly accurate descriptions of the wave determine a well-controlled detector reading.
This is an idealized scalar wave model, not a calibrated instrument or a model of gravitational-wave detection.

general.heading: What information are we given?
paragraphs: Compare two descriptions. The first says that the approximations will eventually settle down. The second also gives an error schedule: for any requested accuracy, it tells us how far to go.
The second description contains extra information. Watching a finite number of approximations agree cannot, by itself, provide that guarantee about every later approximation.

general.heading: What follows?
paragraphs: With the error schedule supplied, the model lets us construct an approximation to the detector reading with controlled error. Without it, the assertion that an appropriate completed reading always exists uses a stronger set of mathematical assumptions in the formulation studied here.
The surprise is where the extra difficulty sits: it is already present in finding a limiting amplitude before the wave moves. Complicated dynamics are not responsible.

general.heading: Why this matters—and its limits
paragraphs: A prediction depends on how its inputs are specified, not only on its equation. This example makes one hidden assumption visible: whether convergence information is part of the data.
It does not show that a physical detector needs stronger logic, nor that every prediction from a wave equation is difficult. It is a comparison of two carefully defined mathematical tasks.

physics.heading: The observable
paragraphs: Take mean-zero left- and right-moving scalar profiles on the unit circle. A fixed periodic tent function h defines Oₚ(t)=∫h(x)[a(x−t)+b(x+t)]dx. Translation supplies the dynamics; spatial smearing supplies a bounded observable.
The model is deliberately simple enough that source representation can be isolated from dynamical complexity.

physics.heading: Two source contracts
paragraphs: Both formulations give bounded rational step-pair approximants satisfying a Cauchy promise in the energy metric. One also supplies a function choosing the index needed for each tolerance. The rate-free formulation supplies no completed state or convergence oracle.

The output is a continuous observable represented by polygonal approximations with a prescribed error rate. A completed input state would already provide missing information and would change the question.

physics.heading: The comparison
paragraphs: With a supplied rate, observable reconstruction is provable over RCA₀. The rate-free existence principle is equivalent over that base to ACA₀, arithmetic comprehension. This is a logical classification of the represented reconstruction problem.
The reversal needs only a fixed spatial profile and the detector at t=0. It therefore does not attribute the stronger requirement to propagation, infinitely many excited modes or chaotic dynamics.

physics.heading: Physical interpretation
paragraphs: The useful lesson is to distinguish finite numerical data, an error-controlled state description, and a bare existence claim. The theorem classifies the last-to-output step for one input contract.

No calibration, stochastic noise model, empirical comparison or full gravitational-field reconstruction is established. The finite detector-recovery benchmark addresses a different question: prediction intervals from specified measurements and an energy bound.

mathematics.heading: Objects and representations
paragraphs: Let D consist of rational periodic step pairs p=(a,b), each component of mean zero. Use the squared distance d(p,p′)²=∫[(a−a′)²+(b−b′)²]. A fixed tent function defines a bounded linear observable of translated profiles.

The input is a coded sequence in the unit ball of D satisfying the ordinary Cauchy condition. The output is a fast uniform Cauchy sequence of rational periodic polygons representing the limiting observable.

mathematics.heading: The missing function
paragraphs: The Cauchy promise has the form ∀k ∃N ∀m,n≥N: d(pₘ,pₙ)²≤2⁻²ᵏ. A modulus supplies a function μ(k) witnessing the existential indices. It is not part of the rate-free input.

RCA₀ supports the coded rate-supplied construction. ACA₀ adds arithmetic comprehension: existence of sets specified by arithmetic formulas. The question is what is needed to obtain the output when only the promise is given.

mathematics.heading: The theorem and its mechanism
paragraphs: Writing WR for the specified rate-free principle, the comparison is RCA₀ ⊢ WRμ and RCA₀ ⊢ (WR ↔ ACA₀). The quantifier is “for every input there exists an output”; no higher-type uniform selector is asserted.

The upper bound extracts suitable indices with arithmetic comprehension. For the reverse implication, a fixed profile transfers scalar limiting-amplitude information to one detector value at time zero. The familiar completeness phenomenon is realized in an explicit wave-observable representation.

mathematics.heading: Scope of verification
paragraphs: Finite rational inequalities and the reduction witnesses have independent computational checks. The infinite reverse-mathematical argument is a human proof, not a proof-assistant-checked theorem.
Neither RCA₀ as a representation-independent weakest base for wave physics nor a general requirement for ACA₀ in physical measurement follows. The exact coding is part of the statement.

specialist.heading: Statement
paragraphs: Over RCA₀, WR ↔ ACA₀ for the rate-free observable reconstruction principle on unit-bounded ordinary-Cauchy sequences of rational mean-zero chiral step pairs. The supplied-modulus version WRμ is provable in RCA₀.

Prerequisites: second-order arithmetic and represented analysis. The scalar completeness reversal is standard; the contribution is its realization in this fixed observable together with the matched rate-supplied formulation.

specialist.heading: Input/output contract
paragraphs: Inputs provide the ordinary Cauchy promise in the squared L² pair metric, without a modulus, completed energy-state name or oracle. Outputs are polygonal names satisfying ‖Aₗ−Aₖ‖∞≤2⁻ᵏ for l≥k, whose limit is the ordinary uniform limit of the input observables.

WR is a second-order ∀input ∃output assertion. Rational-time evaluation and finite polygon comparisons express the required conditions without assuming a function space as a set of all points or a higher-type choice functional.

specialist.heading: Proof mechanism
paragraphs: Uniform boundedness of the observable controls passage from data to output. Arithmetic comprehension supplies modulus information for the upper bound. The reverse reduction is already supported on one fixed spatial profile and a fixed tent detector at t=0.

Thus the lower bound is an amplitude-completion effect, not a propagation obstruction. Read the linked proof for the exact coding and both implications; finite witness checks do not formalize the infinite theorem.

specialist.heading: Boundaries and related material
paragraphs: No representation invariance, general causal Green construction, physical axiom requirement or experimental detector claim is established. Supplying a completed state would alter the input and invalidate the purported rate-free comparison.

The atlas ladder records separate analytic extensions. The finite detector-recovery benchmark is an optimal-recovery specialization under measurement and energy constraints, not evidence for a new reversal.
